Widespread cirrus is covering the Marianas from remnants of this
mornings thunderstorms over Tinian and Saipan. Weak, isolated showers
remain this afternoon but are expected to ramp back up slightly
overnight as proximity to Invest 92W is producing an unstable 
atmosphere. Therefore, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
are in the forecast for tonight through tomorrow. Shower coverage is 
expected to increase Thursday night through Friday as Invest 92W 
passes over the Marianas, bringing the potential for heavy rainfall 
and gusty winds with any thunderstorms that develop. As discussed in 
the Tropical Systems section below, Invest 92W remains unlikely to 
pass through the Marianas as a tropical storm. However, the Marianas 
should still expect increasing showers, isolated thunderstorms, 
building seas and surf, and stronger winds. Afterwards, a ridge of 
high pressure will fill in once 92W passes, bringing drier conditions
to the Marianas.

Marine...
Light to moderate east winds and combined seas of 3 to 5 ft are 
expected tonight. Seas are increasing slightly and are expected 
to peak Thursday night at 5 to 6 ft with the passage of Invest 
92W. Isolated thunderstorms are possible for the next few days. Gusty
winds are possible with these thunderstorms Thursday night through
Friday. There will be a moderate risk of rip currents along
east facing reefs of the Marianas through at least Friday. A 
moderate risk of rip currents will develop along north facing reefs by 
tomorrow due to wrap around from the east swell.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 92W continues to advance toward the Marianas. 92W is 
currently centered north of Chuuk near 11.7N 151.6E, moving WNW at 
around 12 mph. Invest 92W has upgraded from a low to medium, meaning
development is now expected, but not within the next 24 hours. 92W 
continues to show disorganized convection around the center. 92W 
will continue to move west-northwest, moving over the Marianas 
sometime between Thursday evening and Friday. Latest model guidance 
are all in fairly good agreement that Invest 92W will remain fairly 
weak as it moves through the Marianas. Based on model guidance and 
latest satellite trends, 92W is most likely to move through as a 
disturbance or tropical depression, with a tropical storm remaining
unlikely. 92W is expected to strengthen more after moving west of 
the islands. Models show some spread in the direction of movement, 
with variations being from south of Guam to near Saipan, with a
southern track being more likely. Stay tuned as we monitor Invest 
92W for signs of strengthening faster than currently expected.

Eastern Micronesia...
The NET (Near-Equatorial Trough) is positioned across the area as it
stretches east from Pohnpei to Majuro, where it transitions into an
ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone). This feature has been a good
focus for scattered to occasionally numerous showers at Kosrae and
Majuro, with Pohnpei seeing more of the scattered shower variety. A
few thunderstorms have been mixed in from time to time, mainly near
Kosrae and Majuro. Additionally, 925mb (just above the surface near
1500 feet) showed a circulation west of Majuro. This will aid in low
to mid level convergence, and with the "nocturnal" (nighttime)
climatological increase in shower coverage that we typically see, we
opted to go with categorical rainfall coverage (80 percent and above
probabilities) there. Some locally heavy rainfall and isolated wind
gusts to 30 knots could occur, but temporal and areal coverage was
insufficient to include in the forecast at this time.

As this wave heads west over the next few days, Pohnpei and Majuro 
may see increasing rainfall potential. All in all, it looks like an 
unsettled, and at times wet, period will continue for the next 
several days. As for mariners, look for seas of 3 to 5 feet, and
winds will mainly be light to gentle.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau, Yap a gentle trade-wind pattern has set up over the
western half of the region. A few weak trade-wind troughs are
anticipated to bring a few light isolated showers over the next few
days. Showers may pick up over the weekend as the Near-Equatorial
Trough (NET) may reinvigorate bringing showers back to the region. 

Chuuk is situated between a weak trade-wind convergence to the north
and the NET to the south. Satellite trends show a clear patch over 
Chuuk lagoon, this is expected to change. Around midnight, showers 
are expected to build back during the diurnal maxima. A pattern of 
isolated showers during the day and scattered showers at night are
expected to hold through the rest of the work week. Then for the 
weekend the NET is expected to flex northward and bringing showers 
through the beginning of next week.

Benign sea conditions are expected to continue. Latest altimetry 
shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet across the region. Palau and Yap
